chunks: Inverting and non-inverting op-amp circuits. The question: Draw an inverting/non-inverting opamp circuit.
There are two basic ways to wire an op-amp as an amplifier. In the inverting circuit, the signal goes to the minus input through a resistor and the output is flipped.
In the non-inverting circuit, the signal goes straight to the plus input and the output has the same sign. In both, two resistors set the gain.
Think of two ways to use a lever. In one, you push the input end down and the other end goes up. That is the inverting amp.
In the other, the output end moves the same way as your hand, but always at least as far. That is the non-inverting amp, which cannot give a gain below 1.
Plus input grounded, signal into the minus node through R in , feedback R f from output to the minus node. The dot marks the summing node where I in meets I f .
Inverting amplifier: gain -R f over R in . Output has the opposite sign. Non-inverting amplifier: gain 1 plus R f over R g . Output has the same sign.
Virtual short: both inputs at the same voltage. Feedback resistor ( R f ): connects the output back to the minus input. Input impedance: how much the circuit loads its source.
Use R f equals 100 kilohms and 10 kilohms for the other resistor, with V in equals 0. 1 volts. The inverting amp has gain -100 over 10 equals -10 , so the output is -1. 0 volts.
The non-inverting amp has gain 1 plus 100 over 10 equals 11 , so the output is plus 1. 1 volts.
The inverting circuit loads the source with 10 kilohms, while the non-inverting one barely loads it at all. That is the whole idea.
"Inverting: plus input to ground, signal through R in into the minus node, R f from the output back to that node. The minus node is a virtual ground, so gain is -R f over R in .
Non-inverting: signal on the plus input, and R f and R g form a divider from output to ground feeding the minus input.
The virtual short makes V out(R g over (R g plus R f)) equals V in , so gain is 1 plus R f over R g .
Inverting has input impedance R in and can attenuate; non-inverting has very high input impedance and gain of at least 1."
